m0054.summary: King Carlos thanks the Queen, then in Paris, for her telegram and says all is well; in code he tells her she may give [something] but only after arranging it with Rosa (probably the Portuguese minister in Paris) and after the French government has been spoken to. The children kiss her hand.
m0054.en:
Thanks for your telegram. Here everything and everyone very well. You may give [it], but only after having arranged it
with Rosa and after she has spoken with the French Government. The little ones kiss your hand. I embrace you. Carlos.

Notes. The telegram is in French with one coded sentence in Portuguese. The coded sentence is taken from the decode
of the time on the card m0060; the French words are in clear on the telegram. "Podes dar" has no object in the
decode; what is to be given is not said. "ella" (she) has no clear antecedent in the telegram. "Rosa" is probably
Tomás de Sousa Rosa, then Portuguese minister in Paris [our identification, not checked].

m0058.summary: King Carlos tells the Queen that all are well, that he has written to her at Malta, and sends his love and the children's greetings. Fits her Mediterranean cruise of spring 1903.
m0058.en:
Here everyone and everything well. [I] have written to you at Malta. [I] embrace you, and the little ones greet
everyone. Carlos.

Note. "salue" is singular as written. The line can also be read "[I] embrace you and the little ones; greet everyone
[from me]". The mention of Malta fits the Queen's Mediterranean cruise of spring 1903 (m0056 reaches her on
board the yacht Amelie at Oran on 5 March 1903).

m0056.summary: Code telegram of 86 taxed words to Queen Amélie on board the yacht Amélie at Oran; no decode found.

snip.cap: The undated telegram m0058: 12 code groups and “03”, with the decode written below them: “Ici tous et tout bien t’ai écrit à Malte”
snip.credit: Arquivo Nacional Torre do Tombo, PT/TT/CAM/M12, image m0058, via DigitArq

system: Telegraphic code of five-digit groups over 10000-99999 with a short group '03'; words and syllables (the decoder writes 'Po-des', 'Ros-a'); not alphabetical (ter 38564, com 58215).
